findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are hardcoded in plaintext as Lambda environment variables, committed to source control and visible to anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration. This leaks long-lived credentials and enables account compromise.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so Lambda environment variables (which here contain secrets) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key rather than a customer-managed CMK, providing no separate access control over the secrets at rest.

The function has no vpc_config, so it runs outside any VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or network ACL controls, increasing exfiltration attack surface for a function handling credentials.
No code_signing_config_arn is attached, so unsigned or tampered deployment packages can be deployed to the function without integrity verification.
The function uses nodejs12.x, an end-of-life runtime that no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment unremediated.
